description: We are a team of BSCS students from SZABIST University building EarthGuard, an AI-powered disaster management solution. Our goal is to use NASA Earth observation data to help detect, predict, and respond to natural disasters faster. We are looking for teammates with skills in AI/ML, data analysis, design, or Earth science.
summary: EarthGuard is an AI-powered disaster management mobile app built with Flutter. It uses NASA Earth observation data, including MODIS and VIIRS satellite fire hotspot detections, to help identify and monitor disaster events such as wildfires in near real time. Because MODIS and VIIRS report hotspots differently, EarthGuard brings both sources together and uses AI to filter duplicate and unreliable detections, so users see clearer and more consistent hotspot information. The app sends timely alerts and shows affected areas on a map, helping communities and emergency responders react faster and make better decisions. Disasters cause major loss of life and property, especially in regions with limited early warning, and EarthGuard makes NASA's open satellite data easy to access on any smartphone, supporting safer and more resilient communities on Earth.
details:
What it does: EarthGuard is an AI-powered disaster management mobile app. It takes NASA MODIS and VIIRS satellite fire hotspot data, harmonizes the two sources, and uses AI to filter duplicate and unreliable detections. Users see a clear, consistent view of active hotspots on a map and receive timely alerts for their area.

How it works: Hotspot detections are fetched from NASA open data (FIRMS), matched across MODIS and VIIRS by location and time, and scored by an AI model for reliability. Confirmed hotspots are shown on an interactive map with severity and time information, and nearby users are notified.

Benefits and impact: Early and trustworthy hotspot information helps communities and emergency responders react faster, reduce loss of life and property, and plan relief efforts. It makes NASA's open satellite data usable on any smartphone, including in regions with limited early warning systems.

Tools used: Flutter and Dart for the mobile app, NASA FIRMS (MODIS and VIIRS) open data, a map SDK for visualization, AI/ML for filtering and scoring detections, and GitHub for version control.

Creativity: Instead of showing two separate data sources, EarthGuard unifies them into one simple view for ordinary users, turning complex satellite data into clear, actionable alerts.

Factors considered: Data accuracy, low internet connectivity, ease of use for non-experts, and fast alerts during emergencies.
